notesForTheArchitect: Acceptance clause 'each sentence in items 1 and 2 names the guard and the log call it describes' is met literally by AGENTS.md, which names both guards by Go symbol. The two settings descriptions name the two log calls by their message text and state the rule the guard enforces, with no Go identifier: that is the plan's decision D4 and a spec departure the plan recorded as unchanged, and the implementer's open question asks the architect to confirm it. Verified as met under that reading; the architect owns the other reading, which would put `reportHookFailure`, `hooksDueSince` and `RepairGrace` into the operator-facing cells.

The issue's item 3 says the helper 'stops only on a final refusal'. The shipped helper stops on no logged failure at all and fails the test at reconcileWait; the one caller that wanted a refusal moved to refusedDispatchStream. That is the plan's decision D1, recorded as a departure and approved in the plan review. Measured here and consistent with it: the ERROR the spec's starting point proposed needs RepairGrace (a minute, internal/bus/nats.go:551) while reconcileWait is 30 s, so it could never fire inside the wait.

Timing margin, measured on a two-core pod: 21 runs of the new test, 1.52-1.89 s in the two batch runs and one 8.06 s outlier, against a 30 s reconcileWait that restarts after the repair. No run came near the bound and none was flaky.
